item.title: Dollar on back foot as US yields, crude prices dip; Aussie buoyed by hawkish RBA
item.description: The US dollar remained under pressure on Wednesday after slipping to a three-week low in the previous session, as a dip in Treasury yields and crude oil prices reduced the currency's appeal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US dollar remained under pressure on Wednesday after slipping to a three-week low in the previous session, as a dip in Treasury yields and crude oil prices reduced the currency's appeal. The Australian dollar hovered close to a three-week high against the greenback with Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser [USN:L1N4660RH TEXT:"saying"] at a Citi conference that the inflation outlook looked "materially worse", leaving him unsure whether the central bank would need to further raise its policy interest rate next month. The Aussie rose 0.1% to $0.7013, just below the previous day's high of $0.7017. The US dollar index , which measures the currency against six peers, was steady at 101.78 after declining 0.2% on Tuesday. Investors have turned to the greenback as an investment haven amid market volatility brought about by war in the Middle East and AI frenzy, partly due to the currency's energy independence. Oil prices eased overnight after touching a five-month high as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. Meanwhile, Wall Street posted a solid session as technology earnings season got underway with SpaceX (SPCX.O) results. Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI rallied on Wednesday. "With equity market sentiment and the growth outlook closely tied to the performance of the major tech firms, their earnings results can have a large bearing on the USD," Carol Kong, economist and currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, wrote in a client note. Amid a "mixed" performance among traditional haven assets this year, "the USD has been the clear standout," she said. "Safe haven demand for the USD is likely to fade once the Middle East conflict ends and energy prices retreat. However, we expect the USD to trend modestly higher in coming months as foreign capital inflows into US markets increase." The greenback was little changed at 158.33 yen , and was steady at $1.1229 per euro and $1.33735 versus sterling . Still, traders remained wary of the euro as France tackles widespread anti-government protests and a worsening fiscal picture. France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to violence last weekend. Among central banks, the US Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan announce policy decisions on consecutive days starting next Wednesday. Traders do not expect changes in interest rates at any of those meetings. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Bank of Canada decide policy on the same day as the Fed, with traders betting on quarter-point hikes by both. The New Zealand dollar slipped 0.1% to $0.5677 on Wednesday, while Canada's loonie was steady at C$1.4064.

item.title: Saluda Medical's shares hit record low on Evoke device recall
item.description: Saluda Medical said on Wednesday it is undertaking a voluntary recall of certain Evoke neurostimulation devices after identifying a manufacturing-related issue, sending shares of the US-based firm to a record low.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Saluda Medical (SLD.AX) said on Wednesday it is undertaking a voluntary recall of certain Evoke neurostimulation devices after identifying a manufacturing-related issue, sending shares of the US-based firm to a record low. Here are the details: The recall relates to certain Evoke Closed Loop Stimulators after Saluda identified a low-incidence issue stemming from a third-party manufacturing process change The manufacturing change resulted in unintended stimulation during charging or an inability to charge an implanted device, the medical devices firm said Saluda said it received 26 complaints out of 3,900 potentially affected implanted devices The Minnesota-headquarted company said the relevant manufacturing process has been corrected and it is removing and replacing affected non-implanted inventory The company is also engaging with the US Food and Drug Administration and other regulators regarding the recall Saluda will also notify physicians and healthcare providers with potentially affected stock and develop a screening process for devices manufactured before the corrective action was implemented The company said it does not expect the action to disrupt product supply, materially affect operations or push costs outside its existing operating earnings and gross margin forecasts Shares of Australia-listed Saluda fell to a record low of A$0.275

item.title: Lutnick announces investment to boost semiconductor production in North Carolina
item.description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Tuesday announced a new investment in North Carolina by Sibelco, an industrial minerals mining and processing company, to support semiconductor production.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Tuesday announced a new investment in North Carolina by Sibelco, an industrial minerals mining and processing company, to support semiconductor production. "We're announcing Sibelco is going to build silicon manufacturing. It's quartz manufacturing. It is basically the foundation of semiconductors," he said during a Trump rally in North Carolina. He did not share details but said the investment would be worth "hundreds of millions of dollars."

item.title: Spain increases lead over US atop FIFA World Rankings
item.description: Spain extended their lead over the United States atop the FIFA/Coca-Cola Women's World Rankings in the latest update on Tuesday after the recent international window concluded.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spain extended their lead over the United States atop the FIFA/Coca-Cola Women's World Rankings in the latest update on Tuesday after the recent international window concluded. La Roja, which have been No. 1 in the rankings since August 2025, played the U.S. twice during the recent window on American soil, pulling out a 2-0 win in Washington, D.C. on Oct. 10 and playing to a 2-2 draw in Chester, Pa., on Oct. 13. The rest of the top nine was unchanged, with Germany, England and Japan completing the top five, followed by France, Brazil, Sweden and Canada. The only new addition to the top 10 in these updated rankings is Denmark, which climbed two spots to 10th, marking the first time it has been in the top 10 since August 2010. Netherlands and North Korea fell one spot each to 11th and 12th, respectively. Malawi, which reached the final of the Women's Africa Cup of Nations over the summer to qualify for its first Women's World Cup next year in Brazil, was the biggest riser, jumping 49 spots to 104th. Egypt, who have lost their last three matches by a combined margin of 15-3, fell the most, dropping 14 spots to No. 113. The FIFA/Coca-Cola Women's World Rankings will next be updated on Dec. 7. --Field Level Media

item.title: Japan shifting to wage-driven inflation phase, finance minister says
item.description: Japan's economy is seeing price rises driven by higher import costs and on the cusp of shifting to a period of sustained inflation driven by rising wages, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: Japan's economy is seeing price rises driven by higher import costs and on the cusp of shifting to a period of sustained inflation driven by rising wages, Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Wednesday. The government's scheduled consumption tax cut and payouts are aimed at cushioning the blow to households from rising living costs, Katayama told parliament. "We are exchanging views with the Bank of Japan on various fronts. I see no gap between the view of the government and that of the BOJ," Katayama said when asked by a lawmaker whether the government's tax cut plan could conflict with the central bank's efforts to combat inflation with interest rate hikes. The BOJ raised interest rates to a 31-year high of 1.25% in September, as the Iran war-induced energy shock, strong global AI demand and higher import costs from a weak yen heighten the risk of underlying inflation overshooting its 2% target. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration plans to cut by two years an 8% consumption tax rate on food items from April next year. Analysts warn the tax cut and the administration's big spending plans could boost demand and contradict the BOJ's efforts to rein in inflation. Katayama said it was true that tax cuts generally work to push up inflation by stimulating demand. "But we will ensure that our responsible and proactive fiscal policy boosts Japan's supply capacity in a way that does not accelerate inflation," she said.

item.title: Oil rises on Middle East supply worries
item.description: Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday on Middle East supply concerns, with traders wary of Red Sea shipping risks and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Colleen Howe
item.content:encoded: Oil prices edged higher on Wednesday on Middle East supply concerns, with traders wary of Red Sea shipping risks and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Brent crude futures rose 85 cents, or 0.78%, to $109.64 per barrel as of 0022 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 76 cents, or 0.78%, to $98.58 per barrel. A supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz while "violating" Iranian regulations, Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said on Tuesday, according to Iranian media. There were at least 18 vessel attacks reported over two weeks, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday. "Attacks on tankers have expanded beyond the Strait of Hormuz," LSEG analysts said in a note. "Iran has been targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings outside of the Arab Gulf, as well as the ship-to-ship transfers that have helped to support Middle East loadings as the conflict has dragged on." The Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for [USN:S8N44M08Y TEXT:"attacks"] on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Saudi Arabia's Riyadh and Abha airports. The death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday [USN:L1N4660GJ TEXT:"rose"] to 73 as fighting intensified. Prices had fallen in the previous trading session after Iran's president discussed [USN:S8N455017 TEXT:"mediation efforts"] in a meeting with Pakistan's army chief in Tehran. On Tuesday, Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69%, at $108.79, after touching a five-month high of $111.99. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled down $1.87, or 1.8%, at $101.79. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi [USN:L1N46611P TEXT:"said"] in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Iran has not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks. In the US, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were working with refiners around the world to [USN:L1N4660LI TEXT:"boost fuel output"] as a diesel shortage has raised prices. US crude oil stockpiles were [USN:L4N4661GA TEXT:"expected to have fallen"] last week along with product inventories, an extended Reuters poll showed on Tuesday. Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that crude inventories fell by about 800,000 barrels in the week ended October 16.

item.title: South Korea October 1-20 exports surge 105% on record chip sales
item.description: South Korea's exports surged 105.4% in the first 20 days of this month from a year earlier, led by record chip sales driven by global AI investment, customs data showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's exports surged 105.4% in the first 20 days of this month from a year earlier, led by record chip sales driven by global AI investment, customs data showed on Wednesday. On a working-day average basis, exports were up 65.9% at a record $4.74 billion. Exports of semiconductors rose 222.5%, accounting for 44.7% of the total. Last month, exports rose 83.7%, the biggest jump since February 1974, with the monthly value topping [USN:L1N45N002 TEXT:"$120 billion"] for the first time.

item.title: China uses crude stockpiles, but rising oil imports may curtail draws
item.description: China tapped its massive crude oil stockpiles for the fourth month in the past five in September as rising refinery processing rates outweighed a slight recovery in oil imports.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: China [USN:L4N46008R TEXT:"tapped its massive crude oil stockpiles"] for the fourth month in the past five in September as rising refinery processing rates outweighed a slight recovery in oil imports. However, the recent pattern of drawing on inventories may end in October, with crude imports poised to recover to the most since March, the last month largely unaffected by the US and Israeli war against Iran, which started on the last day of February. Refineries processed about 530,000 barrels per day (bpd) more than what was available to them from crude imports and domestic oil production, according to calculations based on official data released this week. China does not disclose the volumes of crude flowing into or out of its strategic and commercial stockpiles, but an estimate can be made by deducting the amount of oil processed from the total crude available from imports and domestic output. On this basis, imports of 9.03 million bpd and domestic production of 4.43 million bpd meant refiners had a total of 13.46 million bpd available. Refineries [USN:L4N46508D TEXT:"processed"] 13.99 million bpd, up slightly from August's 13.91 million bpd and the most since March, meaning throughput was 530,000 bpd more than available crude. The September draw on inventories was down from the 640,000 bpd in August, largely reflecting the increase in crude imports from 8.93 million bpd to September's 9.03 million, an increase of 100,000 bpd. Even though China has dipped into stockpiles in recent months, strong builds before the start of the Iran conflict mean that there is still a small surplus of crude for the first three quarters of 2026. Refiners processed 13.73 million bpd in the first nine months of the year, while imports and domestic output totalled 13.97 million bpd, leaving a surplus of 240,000 bpd. This means that despite the dramatic cut in crude imports seen since the start of the Middle East conflict, China hasn't reduced its oil stockpile, which is estimated by analysts to contain at least 1.2 billion barrels. PRICE IMPACT What the world's largest crude importer has done is cut the volume of arrivals in the face of the surge in prices as a result of the war. Global benchmark Brent futures reached a four-year high of $126.41 a barrel on April 30, up significantly from the close of $72.48 the day before the war started as the conflict shut off flows through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway through which about 20% of global crude and refined fuels moved. However, flows through the still-contested waterway have risen in recent weeks as Gulf exporters such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates risk attacks from Iran. This has resulted in Brent dropping to below $80 a barrel in early August, the time when Chinese refiners would have been arranging October-delivery cargoes. Increased availability and moderating prices will result in China's crude imports rising to more than 10 million bpd in October, which would be the most since the 11.79 million recorded in March. China's seaborne imports are estimated by commodity analysts Kpler at 9.02 million bpd for October, a figure that may be revised higher by as more cargoes are assessed by the end of month. In addition to the seaborne arrivals, China receives about 1 million bpd of pipeline imports from Russia and Central Asia. The likely increase in October crude imports may be enough to cover refinery processing, even if run rates recover to more usual volumes around 14.5 million bpd. The rising crude imports are already being reflected in storage data collated by EA Crude Oil Inventories. China's onshore crude inventories rose for a second week in the seven days to October 19, reaching 1.192 billion barrels, up from the 1.189 billion the prior week, the data showed. Onshore stockpiles had reached a record 1.354 billion barrels on May 4, according to the EA data, meaning they have dropped by 162 million barrels since then. However, it's worth noting that they are only down 13 million barrels from the 1.205 billion EA reported for the week ending October 20 last year. This confirms that while China has tapped inventories in recent months, it has barely touched them in annual terms, meaning the country still retains the ability to adjust crude import volumes according to prevailing prices. item.title: Japan's September exports rise 16.7%, helped by chip demand
item.description: Japan's exports in September rose 16.7% from a year earlier, government data showed on Wednesday, as strong demand for semiconductors and AI-related products offset weakness in other sectors.
item.dc:creator: Makiko Yamazaki
item.content:encoded: Japan's exports in September rose 16.7% from a year earlier, government data showed on Wednesday, as strong demand for semiconductors and AI-related products offset weakness in other sectors. The increase marked the 13th consecutive month of gains, following a 19.3% rise in August and falling short of a median market forecast for a 20.1% increase, Ministry of Finance data showed. Solid global investment in artificial intelligence continued to support exports of semiconductors and related equipment. Exports have also been supported by corporate efforts to pass on higher costs through prices. By destination, exports to the United States rose 22.9% in September from a year earlier, while shipments to China increased 8.6%. Imports in September rose 18.9% from a year earlier, compared with economists' median forecast for a 19.6% expansion. Growth in imports slowed from 28% in August due to lower crude oil arrivals after tankers rerouted away from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait when Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia declared a [USN:L4N43N12U TEXT:"naval blockade"] against Saudi Arabia, delaying deliveries into Japan. For October, crude oil procurement is expected to recover to around 100% of the level seen in the same month a year earlier, as tankers travelling via the Suez Canal are expected to arrive, the government has said. Slower imports helped narrow Japan's trade deficit to 536.6 billion yen ($3.39 billion) in September from 1.1 trillion yen in the previous month. It compared with a forecast for a 181 billion yen deficit. The data suggests external demand remains supportive of Japan's economy, although uncertainty over the global outlook continues to cloud prospects for exporters. The Bank of Japan holds a key policy meeting later this month where it will release fresh quarterly growth and inflation forecasts that markets will scrutinise for clues on the timing of the next interest rate hike. ($1 = 158.2600 yen)

item.title: LeBron James begins 76ers era in hostile NYC territory
item.description: LeBron James made his Philadelphia debut against the Knicks in New York's hostile territory on Tuesday, looking to deliver a title to the long-suffering 76ers in his record-extending 24th season before the clock runs out on his career.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: LeBron James made his Philadelphia debut against the Knicks in New York's hostile territory on Tuesday, looking to deliver a title to the long-suffering 76ers in his record-extending 24th season before the clock runs out on his career. The 41-year-old looked to have turned the clock back as he bounded around the court at Madison Square Garden, with the four-time MVP driving interest in the most hotly anticipated contest of the NBA's opening day. The lowest resale ticket price for the game surged to upwards of $2,000, surpassing the total get-in price for every other team's home opener combined, according to resale platform TickPick, as New York's religiously devoted fans found the deepest part of their pockets four months after the team won the title. The fans booed whenever the announcers mentioned James ahead of tipoff, and the team received their championship rings for ending the Knicks' 53-year title drought in June. Philadelphia fans [USN:L6N45K0WO TEXT:"celebrated his arrival"] even before he stepped onto the court, as they hoped the four-time MVP could end the team's 43-year title dry spell. The 41-year-old took a historic pay cut when he joined his fourth franchise, which he is convinced can take the trophy, despite widespread reports that he is managing chronic arthritis in his foot. While the sight of James in the Philadelphia red, white and blue jersey was still surreal for some fans, his moves were all too familiar on Tuesday, as he helped the Sixers to an early lead.

item.title: Equador e Peru se comprometem a enfrentar juntos criminalidade e ameaça climática do El Niño
item.description: Os presidentes do Equador e do Peru se comprometeram nesta terça-feira a trabalhar juntos para combater a “criminalidade transfronteiriça” que atua na região de fronteira e para prevenir os efeitos do fenômeno climático El Niño em ambos os países.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os presidentes do Equador e do Peru se comprometeram nesta terça-feira a trabalhar juntos para combater a “criminalidade transfronteiriça” que atua na região de fronteira e para prevenir os efeitos do fenômeno climático El Niño em ambos os países. Daniel Noboa e Keiko Fujimori assinaram, após uma reunião em Lima, uma série de acordos de caráter econômico e comercial como parte de um processo de integração, após ambos os países terem travado uma breve guerra em meados da década de 1990. “Hoje, a realidade exige de nós decisões firmes e uma cooperação muito mais forte em matéria de segurança para combater com a contundência necessária a criminalidade transnacional”, disse Noboa, após destacar, entre os acordos, um que permite retomar ações militares coordenadas na fronteira comum. O Equador e o Peru aderiram este ano a uma coalizão patrocinada pelos Estados Unidos com o objetivo de combater os cartéis de drogas e o crime transnacional na região. Além disso, ambos os países enfrentam os estragos causados pelo El Niño, um fenômeno natural que ocorre quando as águas superficiais do Pacífico se aquecem mais do que o normal na costa da América do Sul, provocando chuvas intensas em algumas zonas e secas em outras, com impacto em quase todo o planeta. “São desafios enormes e, se somarmos a isso o fenômeno El Niño, acredito que agora, mais do que nunca, somos obrigados a trabalhar juntos e em equipe”, afirmou Keiko Fujimori após o encontro realizado no Palácio do Governo, em Lima. Entre outros acordos, destaca-se o fortalecimento da luta contra a mineração ilegal, segundo a Presidência peruana, principalmente de ouro, que tem crescido na fronteira comum em um momento em que o metal atingiu preços recordes.

item.title: Resíduos fecais contaminam sumidouros e poços de água potável no Estado de Yucatán, no México, diz Greenpeace
item.description: A água de poços e sumidouros no Estado de Yucatán, no México, que os moradores utilizam para beber, está contaminada com bactérias fecais, de acordo com um relatório do Greenpeace publicado nesta terça-feira, que apontou as fazendas de suínos nas proximidades e as águas residuais municipais como prováveis fontes da contaminação.
item.dc:creator: Iñigo Alexander
item.content:encoded: A água de poços e sumidouros no Estado de Yucatán, no México, que os moradores utilizam para beber, está contaminada com bactérias fecais, de acordo com um relatório do Greenpeace publicado nesta terça-feira, que apontou as fazendas de suínos nas proximidades e as águas residuais municipais como prováveis fontes da contaminação. O Greenpeace pediu uma moratória imediata sobre novas operações pecuárias industriais e expansões de fazendas no Estado, berço da antiga civilização maia. “Uma série de indicadores químicos e microbiológicos revela um mosaico complexo de poluição orgânica grave e localizada”, afirmou o relatório. O Greenpeace contratou um laboratório independente para analisar a água em 17 locais próximos à capital do Estado, Mérida, em agosto. Os locais incluíam poços residenciais e agrícolas, pontos de abastecimento comunitários e cenotes — as dolinas naturais que pontilham a península de Yucatán, um dos destinos turísticos mais populares do México. De acordo com o relatório, todas as amostras apresentaram algum grau de contaminação provavelmente ligado a resíduos fecais, e vários locais pareciam fortemente poluídos. O total de bactérias coliformes atingiu o limite máximo do teste em 16 das 17 amostras, e os coliformes fecais, em 13. No entanto, os testes não conseguem indicar se os resíduos vieram de pessoas ou animais, e vazamentos de fossas sépticas e esgoto municipal também podem contribuir para a contaminação. O Greenpeace afirmou que os resultados levantam “questões críticas de responsabilidade” sobre as fazendas de suínos nas proximidades. O governo do Estado de Yucatán não se pronunciou, enquanto a Comissão Nacional de Águas do México (Conagua) não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. A Associação de Criadores de Suínos de Mérida também não respondeu ao pedido de comentário da Reuters. Sem rios à superfície, as águas subterrâneas são a única fonte de água doce de Yucatán, e o leito rochoso de calcário poroso da região permite que os poluentes se infiltrem rapidamente no aquífero. O relatório indicou que cerca de 30% dos moradores locais bebem água retirada diretamente de poços e sumidouros. O Greenpeace, citando sua pesquisa de 2020, afirmou que apenas 22 das 257 fazendas de suínos em Yucatán possuíam um estudo de impacto ambiental em vigor. A organização também constatou que 43 dessas fazendas operavam dentro de áreas naturais protegidas. Um relatório da ONU publicado em julho constatou que há mais de 500 fazendas industriais de suínos em todo o Estado de Yucatán, com mais de 50 mil animais, muitas delas localizadas próximas às terras e territórios dos povos indígenas. Marcos Orellana, ex-relator especial da ONU e autor do relatório, afirmou que resíduos e produtos químicos provenientes das fazendas industriais “chegam muito rapidamente” às águas que as comunidades utilizam para banhar-se, cozinhar e beber. Ele disse que a maioria das fazendas não possui as licenças exigidas e que as iniciativas do governo regional “continuam insuficientes”. “A contaminação das águas que sustentam a cultura maia há milênios provém predominantemente das operações industriais de criação de animais”, disse Orellana. Mas Antonio Zumarraga, vice-presidente do Observatório Científico Cidadão da Água de Yucatán, defendeu a indústria suinícola local, dizendo que o setor investiu em tratamento de água e apoia programas de conservação. Ele culpou as autoridades locais pela falta de ação. “É uma questão que, enquanto não tiver peso político para o governo, eles não farão nada a respeito”, disse Zumarraga.

item.title: SafePay ransomware group has targeted hundreds this year, US agencies say
item.description: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said on Tuesday that about 600 victims were affected this year by SafePay, one of the world's most active ransomware groups.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said on Tuesday that about 600 victims were affected this year by SafePay, one of the world's most active ransomware groups. Victims range from the Americas to Australia, CISA said in a joint statement with other agencies, including the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the US Secret Service. SafePay gains network access by accessing compromised credentials and targets "known vulnerabilities" in internet-facing devices, the statement said. The group then steals data and encrypts systems, pressuring victims to pay by threatening to publish the stolen information. In some cases, according to the statement, the group calls victims directly. "SafePay actors have already targeted more than 600 victims worldwide across multiple critical infrastructure sectors," said Brett Leatherman, the assistant director of the FBI's cyber division.

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla's Terafab targets 2028 for volume chip production, Musk says
item.description: The chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX and Tesla called Terafab aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028, Elon Musk said on a SpaceX conference call on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Max Cherney
item.content:encoded: The chip manufacturing joint venture between SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) called Terafab aims to reach volume production by the third quarter of 2028, Elon Musk said on a SpaceX conference call on Tuesday. "I put big error bars on this because we don't know if we will actually achieve this or not," Musk said, referring to the timeline. The timeline is a rough schedule for a project that aims to produce 1 terawatt a year of computing power for AI and robotics, on a schedule Musk himself called "very aggressive." In the United States, cutting-edge logic factories can take three or more years to build. Musk has described the planned complex in Texas as combining advanced manufacturing, packaging and testing of both advanced logic and memory chips in one facility. On Tuesday, Musk said that internally, Terafab aims to have a first test chip, using static random-access memory (SRAM) circuits, functional in roughly May or June of next year at the Terafab research facility in Austin. Chip manufacturers commonly fabricate SRAM circuits as a method of refining manufacturing process development. MUSK CAUTIONS ON AMBITIOUS DATES Musk has a history of setting timelines that his companies have missed. The SpaceX CEO described the Terafab timeline as the company's aspiration and said the dates are "very aggressive." "Let's just say that outcome of achieving volume production is at least in the set of possible outcomes for Q3 or Q4 of '28," Musk said. "So these are obviously like insanely fast time frames for chip production." EQUIPMENT ACQUISITION CHALLENGE On the SpaceX conference call, a sell-side analyst asked Musk whether SpaceX had placed orders for the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines produced only by the Dutch company ASML. The EUV machines are necessary to produce the most cutting-edge chips made by Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) . Musk did not answer the question directly and said, "Now these were very aggressive dates, and we're very appreciative of ASML and all of our other suppliers in accelerating equipment deliveries in order to achieve this outcome." One of the challenges Terafab faces is acquiring enough of the complex, expensive semiconductor manufacturing equipment from ASML or American suppliers such as Applied Materials (AMAT.O) and KLA (KLAC.O) . Intel (INTC.O) [USN:L4N40Q0ZN TEXT:"said in April"] that it would join the Terafab project to help accelerate Terafab's goals. Intel also posted a photo of CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Musk shaking hands, saying it hosted the world's richest man at its campus that month. The companies have not revealed how the collaboration would function in practice. Earlier this month, [USN:L6N45T08J TEXT:"Musk said"] there had been discussions about potential cooperation with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (2330.TW) , the world's largest advanced chip manufacturer. But Musk later said Terafab is committed to running the facility itself.

item.title: Japan's late charge seals third straight world team crown, Russians claim silver
item.description: Japan saved their best for last to retain the men's team crown at the world gymnastics championships on Tuesday, overtaking Great Britain and China in the closing stages before seeing off Russia for gold.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan saved their best for last to retain the men's team crown at the world gymnastics championships on Tuesday, overtaking Great Britain and China in the closing stages before seeing off Russia for gold. The Olympic champions entered the final two rotations with work to do but produced a superb finish, scoring 251.928 to secure a third consecutive world team title and add another major gold to their triumph at the Paris Games two years ago. Russia, competing as "World Gymnastics 2", marked their return to major international team competition with silver on 250.329, while China took bronze with 249.193. Russia's silver marked a significant return to the world stage after almost four years on the sidelines following the country's invasion of Ukraine. Russian athletes initially returned to international competition as neutrals, and at these championships the team are competing without the Russian flag or anthem. World Gymnastics allows host countries to determine how Russian teams are treated, with Russia competing as a neutral team at these championships. Britain looked poised for victory after leading through four rotations, but their challenge unravelled on the parallel bars when Courtney Tulloch fell. Daiki Hashimoto, the 2020 Olympic and three-times world all-around champion, made certain there would be no late collapse for Japan. He finished the night in style, sticking his dismount on the high bar to seal gold. The top three teams earned spots in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

item.title: Intuitive tightens 2026 robotic-surgery procedure growth forecast; shares fall
item.description: Intuitive Surgical on Tuesday tightened its 2026 forecast for growth in procedures performed using its da Vinci robotic surgery systems.
item.dc:creator: Sahil Pandey
item.content:encoded: Intuitive Surgical (ISRG.O) on Tuesday tightened its 2026 forecast for growth in procedures performed using its da Vinci robotic surgery systems. Procedure growth is a key measure for Intuitive as surgeries performed using its da Vinci systems generate recurring sales of instruments and accessories, its largest revenue segment. The medical-device maker, whose shares fell about 7% in extended trading, expects worldwide da Vinci procedure growth to be closer to the midpoint of its 14% to 15% forecast range. Its prior view was 13.5% to 15.5% US da Vinci procedure growth was 10% in the third quarter, while growth outside the US was 20% Intuitive plans to roll out its Extended Use Program, designed to reduce instrument costs and broaden access to robotic-assisted surgery, and expects the US to be its first market, pending regulatory clearance Third-quarter adjusted profit was $3 per diluted share on revenue of $3.05 billion, compared with estimates of $2.64 and $2.91 billion, respectively, according to data compiled by LSEG Intuitive continues to monitor lower Affordable Care Act enrollment, changes to Medicaid eligibility and potential changes to the 340B drug-pricing program, CFO Jamie Samath said In July, Intuitive said the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies had a [USN:L4N43J0NN TEXT:"modest adverse impact"] on US procedure growth

item.title: UK employer pay awards edge up to 3.1%, Brightmine says
item.description: Pay settlements by British employers edged up in the three months to the end of September but there was little sign of a shift in wage trends, human resources data firm Brightmine said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pay settlements by British employers edged up in the three months to the end of September but there was little sign of a shift in wage trends, human resources data firm Brightmine said on Wednesday. The median pay award by employers rose to 3.1%, up from 3.0% in the previous three-month periods to August and July but lower than the pace of increases seen earlier this year. On Tuesday, [USN:L8N46608R TEXT:"official data showed"] private sector wage growth rose for the first time since the end of 2024, adding to the case for a Bank of England interest rate hike in November. Below are details from the survey: Most pay deals did not exceed those given a year earlier Pay awards were expected to stay at 3% in 2027 Higher employer social security contributions are constraining employers An increase in the minimum wage could also stretch budgets Brightmine analysed 42 pay settlements between July 1 and September 30 covering more than 650,000 employees.

item.title: Barcelona take heart despite third straight defeat to PSG
item.description: Midfielder Pedri said before Barcelona's clash with Paris St Germain that the game would show where his team stood in Europe. Their 4-2 defeat on Tuesday suggested Hansi Flick's side are not yet among the continent's elite, but they may be closing the gap.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Midfielder Pedri said before Barcelona's clash with Paris St Germain that the game would show where his team stood in Europe. Their [USN:L6N4661C4 TEXT:"4-2 defeat"] on Tuesday suggested Hansi Flick's side are not yet among the continent's elite, but they may be closing the gap. Barcelona arrived in Paris with a perfect record across all competitions this season, yet there was a feeling in Spain that PSG would provide a truer measure of their credentials in the Champions League, the one major trophy that has eluded them under Flick. Their attacking firepower has overwhelmed opponents in LaLiga, but doubts remain over whether Flick's aggressive approach leaves Barcelona exposed against stronger European sides. Those concerns resurfaced when Desire Doue opened the scoring in the 38th minute. Barcelona had mitigating circumstances. Marc Bernal was a surprise starter in midfield, instead of Rodri, while Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde were missing from the defence through injury. Joan Garcia's eight first-half saves underlined PSG's greater comfort with the frantic tempo Barcelona sought to impose. After another excellent Garcia save to open the second half, Barcelona clicked into gear and began to take control. Xavi Espart, 19, marked his first Champions League start with the equaliser, displaying composure beyond his years. Lamine Yamal also emerged as the focal point of Barcelona's attack after a subdued first half. PSG struggled to live with his incisive passing and looked vulnerable as Barcelona enjoyed more of the ball until Lucas Hernandez's set-piece goal in the 72nd minute. Eventually, PSG delivered one too many blows and Barcelona's resistance was broken. Their confidence remained intact though. "Despite today’s result, we competed well," said captain Raphinha on Movistar+, adding that "it was a good test and shows that we can compete." Flick struck a similarly upbeat note. "We need to analyse the match, but I saw some very good things and things that we should build upon. I don’t want to be negative; I’m feeling positive," he said. The German manager acknowledged that PSG were the better side. However, Barcelona avoided some of the failings that undermined their previous two European campaigns under him, particularly indiscipline and vulnerability to counter-attacks. A third successive defeat by Luis Enrique's PSG will sting, but Barcelona return from Paris with reasons to believe they are moving closer to the European champions.

item.title: Governo Trump diz ter revogado mais de 300 mil vistos
item.description: O governo do presidente Donald Trump revogou mais de 300 mil vistos dos Estados Unidos durante seu segundo mandato, informou o Departamento de Estado nesta terça-feira, enquanto o governo federal dá continuidade à sua ampla ofensiva contra a imigração.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: O governo do presidente Donald Trump revogou mais de 300 mil vistos dos Estados Unidos durante seu segundo mandato, informou o Departamento de Estado nesta terça-feira, enquanto o governo federal dá continuidade à sua ampla ofensiva contra a imigração. O número revelou uma aceleração no ritmo das revogações de vistos nas últimas semanas. Em uma atualização divulgada em 10 de agosto, o Departamento de Estado havia estimado o número de revogações de vistos desde o início do atual mandato de Trump, em janeiro de 2025, em mais de 175 mil. Trump afirma que sua repressão à imigração e a campanha de deportações visam melhorar a segurança interna. Defensores dos direitos humanos afirmam que a repressão violou o devido processo legal e os direitos à liberdade de expressão, além de ter criado um ambiente inseguro, especialmente para as minorias étnicas, que têm manifestado preocupações com o perfilamento racial. Ao anunciar o número mais recente no X, o porta-voz do Departamento de Estado, Tommy Pigott, disse que o governo Trump “revogou mais vistos em um ritmo mais rápido do que qualquer outro governo na história”. Pigott afirmou que o governo tem “tolerância zero para com estrangeiros que estão aqui com visto e que infringem a lei, cometem fraudes ou prejudicam nossa segurança nacional”. Entre as revogações de vistos particularmente condenadas por defensores dos direitos humanos estão as de manifestantes estrangeiros pró-palestinos que protestavam contra os ataques de Israel — aliado dos EUA — a Gaza e as de estrangeiros por causa de comentários nas redes sociais sobre o assassinato do comentarista conservador Charlie Kirk. Além das tentativas de deportar manifestantes estrangeiros, o governo Trump intensificou a fiscalização nas redes sociais de imigrantes e requerentes de visto. Defensores dos direitos humanos afirmam que o governo tem invocado razões de segurança nacional para perseguir críticos e usado casos isolados de fraude para atingir amplamente comunidades de imigrantes, como a comunidade somali-americana em Minnesota. Embora Trump tenha feito campanha em 2024 com a promessa de coibir a imigração ilegal, seu governo também tornou a imigração legal mais difícil — por exemplo, ao impor taxas onerosas para certos vistos de trabalho.

item.title: Football regulator has ‘absolute power’ to force club owners to sell, says Kogan
item.description: England's new football regulator has the power to order a club owner to sell and could launch its own investigation once Manchester City's appeal against a verdict that it committed 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules is resolved, its chair David Kogan said.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: England's new football regulator has the power to order a club owner to sell and could launch its own investigation once Manchester City's appeal against a verdict that it committed 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules is resolved, its chair David Kogan said. Kogan, chair of the Independent Football Regulator, said it would assess the conduct of owners and senior club officials against its own tests and had the authority to remove an owner if they failed to meet them. "We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety," Kogan told The Rest Is Football podcast. Asked by co-host Alastair Campbell whether an owner could refuse, Kogan said: "No, no, no. We've got absolute power to do so." The Independent Football Regulator was established in July 2025 to safeguard the financial sustainability of English football, with powers to oversee club owners and directors and intervene when clubs are at financial risk. The regulator's powers have come into focus amid Manchester City's appeal against the verdict. Kogan said the regulator would wait for that process to play out before deciding whether to mount a separate investigation. "I am not going to get pushed into making any judgement on this until we've seen all of those questions being answered and then we will have to decide whether we're going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we're going to do," he said. "And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake." Kogan said the regulator's role differed from the league's because its focus would be on the individuals running clubs rather than imposing sporting sanctions on the clubs themselves. "We would judge against the tests of ownership and senior directors and executives. We would judge the actions of those individuals," he said. "We're not there, we can't, unlike the Premier League, who obviously can take action against the club in terms of fines or points deduction or whatever it may be." Kogan also said the regulator could not automatically prevent a state-backed takeover of an English club under the legislation establishing it. "That legislation does not allow for us to block something just because it's a Norwegian sovereign fund, as an example," he said. "But we're bound very much by the way the legislation has been written, which doesn't preclude that from happening." PREMIER LEAGUE-EFL DEAL In the wide-ranging interview with Gary Lineker and Campbell, Kogan also revealed details of proposals aimed at resolving the long-running dispute over the distribution of money between the Premier League and English Football League. "The Premier League is now talking about more than doubling the amount it pays every year in what are known as solidarity payments, money flowing down to the other (lower) leagues," Kogan said. Under the proposed arrangement, parachute payments to clubs relegated from the Premier League would be reduced while funding flowing into the Championship would increase substantially, Kogan said. He said the changes would narrow the financial gap between relegated clubs receiving parachute payments and their Championship rivals, making the division more competitive. Kogan also questioned the amount being spent on agents, saying fees had surpassed 500 million pounds. "Agents' fees are ridiculous. Over £500 million. It's half a billion pounds," he said. "Hell, I'd much prefer to see it being spent on players." Kogan said another concern was the amount clubs owed one another, which he put at billions of pounds, adding that transfer debt was rising dramatically.

item.title: India's Jio IPO opens for public bids in record $3.2 billion sale
item.description: Public bidding for the $3.2 billion IPO of Jio Platforms opens on Wednesday, testing the appetite for India's largest share sale to date and the first from billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance conglomerate in two decades.
item.dc:creator: Vibhuti Sharma, Aditya Kalra
item.content:encoded: Public bidding for the $3.2 billion IPO of Jio Platforms (JIOP.NS) opens on Wednesday, testing the appetite for India's largest share sale to date and the first from billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance (RELI.NS) conglomerate in two decades. The Jio Platforms IPO will be a major test of global appetite for new share offerings at a time when investors have sharpened their scrutiny of AI-related companies, which some analysts say could see them pivoting away from the technology. With backing from Meta, Google and institutional investors, Jio Platforms is home to India's biggest telecom company with more than 500 million subscribers, making it the world's second-largest telecom operator in a single country after China Mobile. The IPO values Jio Platforms at up to $108.3 billion, potentially making it one of India's biggest companies by market capitalisation when trading starts on October 28, with around a third of the shares on offer reserved for retail investors. Jio Platforms this week [USN:L1N46509C TEXT:"allotted"] shares worth $853 million to global and domestic investors including Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock after the reserved portion for such investors drew bids totalling more than $25 billion. FESTIVE LAUNCH DATE Retail investors, employees and shareholders of Reliance will get to participate in the offering that closes on Friday and has a price range set at 1,065 to 1,119 rupees per share. The IPO is the first from Reliance since 2006 and is bigger than previous major listings such as Hyundai Motor India (HYUN.NS) and National Stock Exchange (NSEI.BO) . Ambani first promised a listing within five years in 2019, and the plans were also delayed [USN:L1N3T60EG TEXT:"in 2025"]. A filing for as early as March was pushed back after the Iran war dampened IPO appetite. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began in 2016 with a bet that Indians would use the internet far more if it cost almost nothing. It rapidly took market share from rivals such as Bharti Airtel (BRTI.NS) and Vodafone Idea (VODA.NS) by offering cheap data and free voice calls. Jio Platforms is pitching its IPO during an ongoing Hindu festive season, which is considered auspicious for purchases, but when Indian markets have remained subdued in recent weeks. Reliance paid its more than 400,000 employees their salaries about 15 days early this month, and the company helped facilitate share account opening services in recent weeks to those interested in applying for the IPO, a person in the industry with direct knowledge of the situation said. Reliance did not respond to a request for comment. Jio Platforms earned about $3.2 billion [USN:L1N46005C TEXT:"in profit"] on $15.5 billion of revenue in the year to March. Around 90% of those figures were attributable to its telecoms business alone.

item.title: AI data center projects boost US warehouse demand and rents, real estate company JLL says
item.description: AI data center construction projects, particularly near Dallas/Fort Worth and Washington, DC, are generating new demand for warehouse space and helped send rents higher in the third quarter, real estate services company JLL said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Baertlein
item.content:encoded: AI data center construction projects, particularly near Dallas/Fort Worth and Washington, DC, are generating new demand for warehouse space and helped send rents higher in the third quarter, real estate services company JLL (JLL.N) said on Tuesday. Companies like Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Meta (META.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) are spending billions of dollars in a race to dominate artificial intelligence, which requires significant electricity to run servers and computer chips that must be cooled to prevent overheating. "Data center expansion is driving outsized industrial demand in major freight hubs such as Dallas/Fort Worth, where suppliers and infrastructure providers are clustering near hyperscale campuses," JLL said in its industrial real estate market report for the third quarter. Average asking rents rose to $10.55 per square foot, up 3.2% from a year earlier, the fastest annual pace of growth since the second quarter of 2024, JLL said. That growth is based on so-called triple-net leases, where tenants pay property taxes, insurance and upkeep of common areas separately from base rent. The expansion of infrastructure-intensive industries is changing the mix of tenants and the location of demand, JLL said, noting that demand from construction, telecommunications and utilities-related tenants increased.

item.title: Grupo México reporta mayores ganancias gracias al aumento de precios y reduce previsión de producción de cobre
item.description: El conglomerado minero y de transporte Grupo México informó que el alza de los precios de los metales contribuyó a que su utilidad neta del tercer trimestre aumentara en más de la mitad con respecto al año anterior, a pesar de una leve disminución en la producción de cobre.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El conglomerado minero y de transporte Grupo México (GMEXICOB.MX) informó que el alza de los precios de los metales contribuyó a que su utilidad neta del tercer trimestre aumentara en más de la mitad con respecto al año anterior, a pesar de una leve disminución en la producción de cobre. El grupo, uno de los principales productores mundiales de cobre, redujo su proyección de producción de cobre para 2026 a 1.028 millones de toneladas métricas, desde la previsión anterior de 1.034 millones de toneladas, una diferencia de 6,000 toneladas. Su producción trimestral de cobre alcanzó las 260,322 toneladas, un 1.9% menos que en el mismo periodo del año anterior, debido a las disminuciones en Perú y en la unidad Asarco en Estados Unidos. Estas cifras más bajas se compensaron parcialmente con un aumento en las operaciones en México. Grupo México indicó que la disminución se debió a la menor ley del mineral en Perú y en Asarco, tal como se esperaba, y agregó que está evaluando opciones para aumentar los volúmenes de producción en Perú. Grupo México informó que su proyecto de cobre Tía María, valorado en 1,100 millones de dólares y que sufrió numerosos retrasos, alcanzó un 49.6% de avance a finales de septiembre, y se prevé que las operaciones comerciales comiencen en el primer semestre de 2028. Los precios del cobre subieron un 30.6% este año hasta el tercer trimestre, mientras que los de la plata se duplicaron con creces. El cobre representa aproximadamente tres cuartas partes de los ingresos de Grupo México. La utilidad neta se situó en 2,000 millones de dólares, un 56% más que el año anterior, y por encima de la estimación de 1,780 millones de dólares de los analistas consultados por LSEG. Los ingresos aumentaron un 38% hasta los 6,330 millones de dólares, superando también la estimación de 5,810 millones de dólares. Las ganancias antes de intereses, impuestos, depreciación y amortización (EBITDA) para el trimestre finalizado en septiembre aumentaron un 50.5% hasta los 3,770 millones de dólares. Además del cobre, la producción de otros metales también se debilitó: la producción de zinc cayó un 7.9% y la de plata un 5.7%. La producción de oro aumentó un 2.4%. Grupo México, controlado por el multimillonario Germán Larrea, es uno de los mayores productores de cobre del mundo a través de su división minera y también opera negocios ferroviarios y de infraestructura en México y otros países latinoamericanos.

item.title: Trump promises cash for fraud tips as he awards right-wing YouTuber
item.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he would reward tipsters who uncover fraud in US government programs, launching the initiative by announcing a cash prize for a conservative online influencer.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he would reward tipsters who uncover fraud in US government programs, launching the initiative by announcing a cash prize for a conservative online influencer. Speaking from the White House Oval Office, Trump said a new Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program would award people an unlimited 1% commission on the fraud reported. The Justice Department described the program differently, saying it would award $10,000 to $30,000 for tips that lead to criminal charges. It said the Treasury Department is committing $25 million toward the program and that the Justice Department would issue the awards in its "sole discretion." The first recipient was [USN:L1N43N016 TEXT:"Nick Shirley"]. Senior administration officials have amplified and credited the 24-year-old pro-Trump YouTuber's viral video alleging some childcare centers in Minnesota were fraudulent as the basis for plans to cut some federal funding to the state. The Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families disputed some of those claims as misleading and exaggerated. But one Minneapolis woman whose childcare center Shirley profiled later pleaded guilty to fraud charges. "There's never been an incentive for anyone to ever expose fraud," Shirley said at the White House. "When you expose fraud, you help save America." Vice President JD Vance, who leads the president's anti-fraud task force, said Shirley had "done more than anybody that I've met recently as a citizen journalist to uncover the fraud" and that "Nick is going to get a financial reward for doing so." A White House official told media outlets that Shirley would get $10,000. It was not immediately clear how Shirley was selected for the prize. The White House, Justice Department and Treasury Department did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment, and Shirley could not immediately be reached. "I will be the arbitrator of all of these decisions," Trump said about who would be paid under the program. "I will be very generous, believe me. We're not looking to save on that." The Republican US president has made allegations of fraud in Democratic-led states a focus of his term in office and has pledged to clean up corruption. He has focused especially on [USN:L1N45U12W TEXT:"Somali immigrants"] in Minnesota, whom he has called "garbage."

item.title: Ngumoha comes of age on breathless Anfield night
item.description: Rio Ngumoha had already been billed as one of Liverpool's brightest young talents, but on a breathless Champions League night at Anfield on Tuesday the 18-year-old delivered the kind of performance that suggested his time had arrived.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rio Ngumoha had already been billed as one of Liverpool's brightest young talents, but on a breathless Champions League night at Anfield on Tuesday the 18-year-old delivered the kind of performance that suggested his time had arrived. With Liverpool trailing by two goals against Villarreal and in desperate need of inspiration, Ngumoha provided it, creating two goals as his side roared back for a dramatic 4-3 victory. "Individually I think I enjoyed myself tonight," Ngumoha said. "As I get older now, affecting games is really important. And today, to get two assists and help the team get the three points, there's nothing more I can ask for." Ngumoha is the youngest Liverpool player to register an assist in the Champions League. "It's the biggest club in the world, and for me to get that record is something special," he said. "So yeah, I'll take it. I'll take it all day." Looking perfectly at home on one of the game's biggest stages, his first intervention saw him show his composure. With Liverpool having pulled one back through Alexis Mac Allister, Ngumoha produced a delightful dinked pass for Ronald Araujo to haul the hosts level on the brink of halftime. If that offered a glimpse of his talent, what followed after the break felt like a coming-of-age moment. Ngumoha took on Sergi Cardona, skipped past the defender and laid the ball on a plate for Mac Allister to tap Liverpool into the lead for the first time. Supporters at Anfield had spent the opening half-hour watching a Liverpool side stumble from one mistake to another. Suddenly, they were watching an 18-year-old take charge. "On the ball, this kid has so much quality," former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge said on the Amazon Prime broadcast. "It is stuff you can't teach. What he does with the ball at his feet, it is God-given ability." Florian Wirtz added a fourth, his first club goal of the season, and although Tani Oluwaseyi's late strike ensured a nervous finish, Liverpool survived to make it three wins from three in Europe. Ngumoha had already made history at Liverpool, becoming the club’s youngest Premier League scorer at Anfield in April, aged 17. He was already the team's youngest scorer thanks to his goal at Newcastle in August 2025 when he was 16. For all the twists in a chaotic seven-goal contest, however, the enduring image was of Ngumoha, and when the final whistle blew supporters celebrated while Duran Duran's "Rio" blasted over the stadium speakers.

item.title: USDA plans to resume imports of Mexican cattle at more ports of entry
item.description: The US Department of Agriculture plans to resume cattle imports from Mexico at two additional US ports of entry, after halting shipments last year in an attempt to keep out the flesh-eating parasite New World screwworm, the agency said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Tom Polansek
item.content:encoded: The US Department of Agriculture plans to resume cattle imports from Mexico at two additional US ports of entry, after halting shipments last year in an attempt to keep out the flesh-eating parasite New World screwworm, the agency said on Tuesday. The USDA plans to restart imports in Columbus, New Mexico, on October 26 and, if conditions for safe trade are in place, in Nogales, Arizona, on November 30, according to a post on X. The block on imports of Mexican cattle helped push US ground beef prices to record highs this year, contributing to rising concerns about food affordability ahead of midterm elections in November. USDA [USN:L1N45A0X4 TEXT:"resumed livestock trade"] in Douglas, Arizona, in August and at a large port in Santa Teresa, New Mexico, in September. Horse imports are expected to resume in Santa Teresa on October 26, the USDA said on X. The agency said it has confirmed 56 US screwworm cases since June, and 5 are active.

item.title: Co-CEO da Netflix diz que "podemos fazer melhor" após previsão fraca
item.description: A Netflix divulgou, nesta terça-feira, uma previsão de lucro para o quarto trimestre abaixo do esperado, dias depois de a pioneira do streaming ter demitido 6% de sua força de trabalho e substituído dois de seus principais executivos de programação.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Richwine, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: A Netflix (NFLX.O) divulgou, nesta terça-feira, uma previsão de lucro para o quarto trimestre abaixo do esperado, dias depois de a pioneira do streaming ter demitido 6% de sua força de trabalho e substituído dois de seus principais executivos de programação. As ações da Netflix caíram quase 6%, para US$64,66, no pós-mercado. As ações haviam caído mais de 40% em um ano antes da divulgação dos resultados. O co-presidente-executivo Ted Sarandos disse que a empresa pretende se concentrar em seu negócio principal de produzir séries e filmes de qualidade para tornar a Netflix um serviço indispensável, e que a recente reformulação da equipe executiva foi um passo nessa direção. "Sei que podemos fazer melhor", disse Sarandos em uma videoconferência após a divulgação dos resultados. "Agora vimos uma oportunidade de levar nosso catálogo a um novo patamar." A receita do terceiro trimestre cresceu 11,8%, para US$12,87 bilhões, em linha com as previsões de Wall Street, mas representou a menor taxa de crescimento em quase três anos. A empresa previu um lucro líquido de US$2,79 bilhões e lucro por ação (EPS) de US$0,67 para o quarto trimestre, abaixo da previsão média dos analistas, de US$3,07 bilhões e US$0,73. A Netflix reduziu sua previsão de receita publicitária para 2026 para cerca de US$2,7 bilhões, ante os cerca de US$3 bilhões previstos anteriormente. Alguns recursos dos produtos publicitários foram lançados um pouco mais lentamente do que o esperado, afirmaram os executivos em sua carta trimestral aos acionistas. A empresa que abalou Hollywood quando começou a transmitir séries de TV e filmes há duas décadas agora enfrenta a concorrência do aumento repentino de audiência no YouTube e no TikTok. A Netflix tem investido em videogames, podcasts e eventos ao vivo para atrair novos espectadores e aumentar o tempo que os assinantes passam na plataforma. Analistas de Wall Street têm questionado como a empresa vai retomar o crescimento. “A Netflix continua sendo uma máquina bem lubrificada e altamente lucrativa, mas está focada em muitas distrações indesejadas”, disse o analista Paolo Pescatore, da PP Foresight. “A empresa precisa voltar ao essencial e se concentrar em conteúdo atraente.” Em seu relatório de resultados, a Netflix afirmou que continuará a expandir sua oferta por meio do licenciamento de mais conteúdo de terceiros. Além disso, ela se concentrará no serviço principal de streaming de TV, filmes e eventos ao vivo e investirá em programas originais que “estimulem conversas, atraiam mais assinantes e nos tornem um serviço ‘indispensável’”, afirmaram os executivos na carta. No terceiro trimestre, o lucro por ação ficou em US$0,87, acima da previsão média de US$0,82 dos analistas consultados pela LSEG. A programação lançada durante o trimestre incluiu “Monstro: A História de Lizzie Borden”, a segunda temporada de “Magnatas do Crime”, a temporada final de “Outer Banks” e um reboot de “Uma Casa na Pradaria”. Na semana passada, a Netflix demitiu 1.000 pessoas, o que representa cerca de 6% de seus funcionários. A empresa substituiu a diretora criativa Bela Bajaria e anunciou que o chefe de cinema, Dan Lin, estava deixando a empresa — sinais de que está redefinindo sua estratégia de programação. A Netflix perdeu neste ano uma disputa pela Warner Bros Discovery e seu vasto acervo de personagens, que foi vendido para a Skydance, liderada por David Ellison . Alguns analistas acreditam que a Netflix poderia buscar outros alvos de aquisição, como a NBCUniversal, depois que a Comcast (CMCSA.O) a desmembrar. A Netflix registrou perdas mensais de assinantes nos EUA ao longo de 2026, sem que fossem relatados ganhos líquidos em nenhum mês até setembro, segundo dados da empresa de análise Antenna. A Antenna acompanha as aquisições de assinaturas nos EUA por meio de fontes como transações com cartão de crédito, mas exclui as assinaturas adquiridas por meio de pacotes de atacado. Um porta-voz da Netflix afirmou que os dados da Antenna “não são representativos do desempenho comercial da Netflix”.

item.title: Suspect in vehicle attack on Australian lawmaker appears in court as police probe motive
item.description: A man who allegedly rammed his car into Australian lawmaker Helen Haines outside her electoral office appeared in court on Wednesday, media reported, as police briefed parliamentarians on their security amid a rise in threats.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose
item.content:encoded: A man who allegedly rammed his car into Australian lawmaker Helen Haines outside her electoral office appeared in court on Wednesday, media reported, as police briefed parliamentarians on their security amid a rise in threats. Doctors amputated one of Haines' legs after the alleged attacker [USN:L1N46510F TEXT:"struck"] her twice with his car in Wangaratta, northeast of Melbourne, on Monday, Australian media and officials said. [USN:L6N4650UX TEXT:"Haines"], an independent lawmaker who has championed causes including climate change and regional housing, remains in critical condition. Anti-terrorism police are among the agencies investigating the incident. While police allege the attack was "targeted," they believe it was an isolated incident. There was no intelligence to suggest any threat to Haines, and the Australian Federal Police received no warning of any imminent danger from the alleged attacker, Commissioner Krissy Barrett told reporters. "What I can say is we didn't have any specific intelligence that would have indicated something as atrocious as happened on Monday afternoon," she said. The alleged attacker was [USN:L1N46600X TEXT:"restrained"] by members of the public at the scene before being arrested and charged on Tuesday with three offences of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a public official. During a brief court appearance on Wednesday, the accused's lawyer said his client suffers from a rare neurological condition called idiopathic transverse myelitis and was also being treated for concussion, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported. There was no application for bail, and the case was deferred until February 4, the report said. Australian media widely reported the alleged attacker as Brendan Nugent, a resident of the rural town of Tarrawingee and part of Haines' electorate, though police have not formally named him. Victoria state police said they could not find any direct past contact between Haines and the accused, with the motive still unknown. "Motivation is one of these things that we absolutely need to explore. His motivation for this, what we allege is a deliberate attack, is very much a centrepiece of the investigation," Victoria Police Chief Mike Bush said. Bush declined to comment on the man's mental health, saying the matter was before the court. Haines had worked in nursing, midwifery and academia before being elected to parliament in 2019 for the rural seat of Indi, which she retained in both 2022 and 2025. 'VIOLENT INCIDENT' Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Wednesday described the attack as clearly a "violent incident," having earlier linked it to a domestic climate of ugly, polarised political debate. "It's a reminder that the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago," he told ABC Radio. Violent attacks on politicians are rare in Australia, where federal lawmakers, state leaders and even prime ministers are often seen shopping, grabbing coffee or attending community events with relatively little security. However, [USN:L4N466030 TEXT:"concerns"] about politicians' safety have grown in recent years amid rising political polarisation, online abuse and threats against elected officials, prompting calls for greater protections while preserving the accessibility that has long characterised Australian politics.

item.title: Australia's Woodside Energy trims 2026 output forecast; third-quarter revenue tops estimates
item.description: Australia's Woodside Energy on Wednesday trimmed the top end of its annual production forecast after lowering expected volumes from its Beaumont New Ammonia plant in Texas, while stronger oil and gas prices helped third-quarter revenue beat estimates.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's Woodside Energy (WDS.AX) on Wednesday trimmed the top end of its annual production forecast after lowering expected volumes from its Beaumont New Ammonia plant in Texas, while stronger oil and gas prices helped third-quarter revenue beat estimates. The country's top independent oil and gas producer now expects annual production of 174 to 181 million barrels of oil equivalent (mmboe), down from its earlier forecast of 174 to 185 mmboe. Shares of the firm fell over 1% in early trading. Woodside said lower expected volumes from Beaumont New Ammonia, tighter timeline for first LNG from the Scarborough project and reduced production at the Okha floating production, storage and offloading vessel weighed on its outlook. The firm said production at its Beaumont New Ammonia facility was constrained to 69% of nameplate capacity during the quarter due to third-party feedstock availability and a roughly 30-day shutdown following a process safety event. It also said it would begin a formal process to reduce its investment in Beaumont New Ammonia following a strategic review of the project. The oil and gas producer reported revenue of $4.28 billion for the three months ended September 30, up from $3.36 billion reported a year ago , beating a Visible Alpha consensus of $4.11 billion. Woodside's average realised price for its products rose 40% from a year earlier to $84 per barrel of oil equivalent, supported by stronger gas hub prices and the impact of LNG portfolio optimisation. Quarterly production volumes fell 9% from a year earlier to 46.2 mmboe, but rose 12% from the previous quarter following higher production from Pluto LNG after maintenance activities were completed in the second quarter. The company had earlier [USN:L4N43U2QX TEXT:"narrowed its annual production forecast in July"], citing strong operational performance. It also maintained its 2026 capital expenditure outlook at $4 billion to $4.5 billion.

item.title: Petrobras avalia como positivo adiamento de audiência sobre Gas Release
item.description: A Petrobras afirmou nesta terça-feira que avalia positivamente a decisão da Agência Nacional do Petróleo (ANP) de postergar para 19 de novembro a realização da audiência pública sobre o Programa de Redução da Concentração no Mercado de Gás Natural (Gas Release).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Petrobras (PETR3.SA) afirmou nesta terça-feira que avalia positivamente a decisão da Agência Nacional do Petróleo (ANP) de postergar para 19 de novembro a realização da audiência pública sobre o Programa de Redução da Concentração no Mercado de Gás Natural (Gas Release). Segundo a companhia, o adiamento "beneficia o bom andamento do processo regulatório, permitindo que o debate público não seja realizado de forma açodada e que sejam melhor avaliados os impactos de curto, médio e longo prazo relacionados ao programa proposto". "A alteração de data permitirá que a decisão final seja mais qualificada, sem comprometer os prazos subsequentes previstos pela agência", disse a estatal, em nota. O Gas Release, afirmou a Petrobras, é um programa de venda compulsória de gás natural, por meio do qual a estatal seria obrigada a vender, por meio de leilões, parte dos volumes de que é titular, com preço mínimo inicial, quantidade e duração a serem definidos pela agência. A Petrobras avalia que a "proposta apenas redistribui volumes já existentes no mercado, com efeitos potencialmente transitórios e sem demonstração suficiente de benefícios duradouros para a concorrência ou para os consumidores".

item.title: Australian central banker says inflation outlook worse, unsure about November rate hike
item.description: A top Australian central banker on Wednesday said tighter monetary policy was working to slow the economy but the inflation outlook had still worsened, leaving him unsure whether interest rates would need to rise further next month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A top Australian central banker on Wednesday said tighter monetary policy was working to slow the economy but the inflation outlook had still worsened, leaving him unsure whether interest rates would need to rise further next month. Speaking at a Citi investment conference, Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the bank's economists were still finalising their quarterly forecasts but the inflation outlook did look "materially worse", in part due to even higher oil prices. Brent [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"last traded"] at $108 a barrel, up from $102 a barrel when the central bank last met three weeks ago and lifted interest rates for a fourth time this year. It was a third higher than what the RBA had forecast in August. "The monetary policy is working, labour market is easing, consumption growth is quite tepid, but there are still pockets of growth and the inflation outlook has deteriorated, so that's a pretty tricky balance," said Hauser. "The challenge that's facing the board is do you do more to tackle high inflation? ... Or do we hold our horses to protect the labour market?" he added. "We're in a world of hard choices, and I think that's the reality here." Hauser said monetary policy could not deal with an oil shock directly, but it did need to make sure that higher costs did not feed through to rising inflation expectations. The central bank meets on November 2-3 to decide whether to raise its 4.60% cash rate for a fifth time this year. Markets now imply around a 40% chance rates will rise to 4.85% next month, up from 30% at the start of the week, and another rate rise is fully priced by May next year. Consumer price data due next week could show headline inflation climbing to 4.0% in the third quarter as the Gulf war stokes fuel costs. Crucially, core inflation is seen holding around 3.5% and uncomfortably far above the RBA's long-term target band of 2% to 3%. Hauser said it was "pretty clear" that the inflation outcome would likely be higher than the RBA had forecast. "Yes, we will study it carefully when we get the final number," he added. "And at the moment, certainly those numbers are causing us to ask whether there's less capacity in the economy than we previously thought." [USN:P8N44M01S TEXT:"Minutes of the RBA's"] last meeting showed the board was still concerned inflation risks lay to the upside, even after lifting rates for a fourth time this year. Since then, [USN:L1N46100L TEXT:"labour data"] have shown [USN:L1N46500C TEXT:"unemployment"] unexpectedly hit a five-year peak of 4.7% in September, while [USN:L1N45M19O TEXT:"house prices"] have fallen faster than policymakers foresaw. Hauser noted the labour market had eased more than expected, and there had been some softening in household demand and the housing market, but still the unemployment rate was among the lowest in G20 countries.

item.title: BOJ to raise rates to 1.50% in December, sticking to quarterly pace: Reuters poll
item.description: The Bank of Japan will raise interest rates in December to 1.50%, following June and September increases, according to a majority of economists in a Reuters poll, keeping up a quicker pace in a campaign that started with just one rate rise a year.
item.dc:creator: Satoshi Sugiyama
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Japan will raise interest rates in December to 1.50%, following June and September increases, according to a majority of economists in a Reuters poll, keeping up a quicker pace in a campaign that started with just one rate rise a year. Rising energy and import costs, worsened by a weak yen and the war in the Middle East, are adding to inflation pressure in Japan, and there are more forecasters expecting at least two more rate rises to 2.0% by the middle of next year. A period of relative stability in the yen, which spent most of the year under crushing selling pressure, triggering interventions from the Japanese authorities as well as the US Treasury, also supports the case for a December increase. [USN:L1N46101P TEXT:"Last week,"] board member Junko Koeda said the central bank should not become overly cautious about raising rates, at their highest in [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"31 years"], given the significant upside risks to inflation. Nearly 70% of economists, 54 of 78, in the October 13-19 survey expected the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.5% this quarter, almost double the share in the [USN:L4N44Z0P0 TEXT:"previous poll"]. Of the 54 respondents who specified a month, about 80% chose December, while only 2% chose the BOJ's next two-day policy meeting, which concludes on October 30. "With rate hikes in the United States and Europe looking likely before year-end, there is a risk that yen selling could accelerate if the BOJ postpones its move until the new year," said Kazutaka Maeda, senior economist at Meiji Yasuda Research Institute. The BOJ is unlikely to raise rates this month, while the [USN:L6N46606V TEXT:"US Federal Reserve"] and the [USN:L6N45U0QU TEXT:"European Central Bank"] are expected to raise borrowing costs in December, separate Reuters polls found. "The economy is not overheating to the extent that would warrant consecutive rate hikes, and price developments are also within the BOJ's expected range," said Takeshi Minami, chief economist at Norinchukin Research Institute. [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"Sources"] have told Reuters many BOJ officials prefer to assess more data on how previous increases have affected financial conditions. RATES TO REACH 2% OR HIGHER Looking into next year, 39 of 65 analysts, or 60%, expected the policy rate to reach 1.75% by end-June, a median unchanged from the September poll.
